comment: Expected negotiation outcomes for every (local policy, peer offer) cell. The harness (scripts/negotiation.py) computes outcomes from the policy rules and compares them against this table; the table is the specification, the code is the implementation. Outcome vocabulary: ACCEPT-HYBRID-<param> (hybrid handshake with that ML-KEM parameter set), ACCEPT-CLASSICAL (classical-only handshake, downgrade event recorded), REJECT (fail closed, no handshake).

policies.allow-classical: Accept the strongest common algorithm; classical is acceptable.
policies.prefer-hybrid: Accept the strongest common hybrid algorithm; fall back to classical only when the peer offers no hybrid algorithm, and record a downgrade event.
policies.require-hybrid: Accept only a hybrid algorithm; reject any peer that offers no hybrid algorithm. Preferred parameter set is ML-KEM-768; 512 and 1024 are acceptable.

rules: R1: The negotiated algorithm must be offered by the peer and permitted by local policy.
R2: Among the permitted common algorithms, the strongest is chosen by the preference order (ML-KEM-768 first as the NIST recommended default, then 1024, then 512, then classical X25519).
R3: Under require-hybrid, a peer offering no hybrid algorithm is rejected; the connection fails closed.
R4: Under prefer-hybrid, a peer offering no hybrid algorithm falls back to classical X25519, and the fallback is recorded as a downgrade event.
R5: The negotiation transcript is the SHA-256 hash of the canonical encoding of the offered algorithm list; any change to the offered list changes the transcript.

R6: A downgrade attack (an attacker removing a hybrid algorithm from the peer's offered list in transit) is detected because the transcript the peer signs differs from the transcript the initiator observed.
